items.title: Expand the contract for debts, strategies and simulation
items.outcome: Debt terms, amortisation schedules, payoff projections, strategy comparison and extra-payment simulation are published as a versioned contract with generated clients, so the server and both clients build against one definition.
items.context: The debt engine is the product wedge and is being implemented server-side, but only the contract skeleton exists. Without published shapes for schedules and projections, each client will invent its own and derived numbers will disagree between surfaces.
scope: Debt entity with its real-world terms including rate type, compounding, fees and minimum payment rules
Amortisation schedule representation with per-period principal, interest and fee components
Payoff projection and strategy comparison responses including the derivation inputs
Extra-payment simulation request and response including the assumptions used
Lender statement reconciliation snapshot shape as defined by the ledger decision record
Error shapes for infeasible plans such as a payment below accruing interest
Hybrid payoff strategy with deterministic transition and tie-break rules
Refinance or consolidation scenario request and response shapes carrying replacement terms, fees, break-even point and assumptions without naming a lender
Optional credit-card statement date, due date, grace period, minimum due and revolving-balance terms
Strategy vocabulary reserving utilization-first, highest-monthly-payment and highest-monthly-interest-cost values
acceptance_criteria: Every monetary field uses the published money representation and no field is a floating point number
A projection response carries enough information for a client to display the derivation without recomputing it
The infeasible-plan case has an explicit error shape rather than an empty schedule
Generated Kotlin and TypeScript clients compile and pass contract verification
The schedule shape supports both fixed and variable rate debts without a client-side branch on debt type
Reconciliation snapshots are distinguishable from computed balances in the response
Hybrid strategy output is reproducible and distinguishable from avalanche, snowball and custom order
Refinance scenarios expose break-even and total-cost deltas with derivation and never contain a product or lender recommendation
Older clients can ignore additive card-cycle fields and unsupported strategy values fail with an explicit capability result rather than a guessed fallback
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 additions with examples for at least one fixed rate and one variable rate debt
security_privacy: No lender account identifier is exposed in full; the contract specifies a masked form
Projection endpoints are tenant scoped and carry no cross-user aggregate
observability: Contract requires a computation identifier on projection responses so a support query can trace a number
tests: Provider and consumer contract verification
Example validation against the schema
Hybrid strategy transition and tie-break contract examples
Refinance break-even and advice-boundary contract tests
Credit-card cycle and advanced-strategy compatibility examples
rollout_rollback: Additive publication under the expand and contract protocol; consumers pin a version
non_goals: Engine implementation, which the api debt tickets own

items.title: Expand the contract for ingestion, deduplication and clarification
items.outcome: Structured capture submission, source precedence, deduplication outcomes, confidence and the clarification queue are published as a versioned contract, so on-device parsers and the server agree on exactly what crosses the boundary.
items.context: The device must send a structured payload and never raw message text, and the deduplication rules must be understandable by the client that shows the result. Without a published shape the privacy promise and the deduplication behaviour are both unverifiable.
scope: Structured capture payload with source, issuer pattern identifier, confidence and parsed fields
Explicit prohibition of raw message text in the schema, expressed so a violation is a contract violation
Deduplication outcome shape naming the surviving record and the reason
Clarification item, question and resolution shapes including rule rollback
Source precedence declaration extensible to future sources without a breaking change
Reuse of the shared confidence-band and dedup-outcome components published by T-CON-10 rather than a second encoding for the automated path
Reuse of T-CON-15 SourceEvent, TransactionCandidate, source_event_id, dedup-decision and persisted-provenance components rather than a second ingestion envelope
Server-computed dedupe_key over canonical structured fields, with the exact construction and key class consumed from T-ADR-CRYPTO-04
acceptance_criteria: The schema has no field capable of carrying raw message text and the examples demonstrate the structured form
A deduplication outcome states which record survived and why, in terms a client can display
A clarification resolution can create, amend or roll back a rule and the shape distinguishes the three
Adding a new capture source requires no breaking change to existing consumers
Generated clients compile and pass contract verification
Confidence is a defined scale with documented thresholds rather than an opaque number
Confidence and dedup outcomes reuse the T-CON-10 components; a parallel encoding for automated ingestion fails contract verification
A single client rendering can display a statement-import duplicate and a cross-channel duplicate without branching on the source
The capture, sync and export schemas reference T-CON-15 source_event_id and contain no raw-derived digest field; a planted raw_hash or message_digest property fails schema verification
The server dedupe_key is output-only and cannot be supplied or overridden by a client
Android and API consumers import the T-CON-15 source_event_id shape; any locally redeclared hash field or divergent identifier fails consumer verification
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 additions with examples per source type
security_privacy: Schema-level prohibition of raw content is the primary privacy control at the boundary
Issuer pattern identifiers are opaque and carry no account information
A digest derived from raw text is treated as raw content and prohibited at every network boundary, even when the original text field is absent
observability: Contract requires a capture identifier so a clarification can be traced to its source event without content
tests: Provider and consumer contract verification
Schema test asserting no free-text content field exists
Negative schema fixtures for raw_hash, message_digest and client-supplied dedupe_key
Android consumer test proving source_event_id is stable across retries while the raw-message HMAC remains local
rollout_rollback: Additive publication; new sources are added additively under the protocol
non_goals: Parser rules and server pipeline behaviour, which their own tickets own

items.title: Expand the contract for billing, entitlements and quota
items.outcome: Plans, entitlements, quota reservation and reconciliation, and subscription lifecycle states are published as a versioned contract, so the entitlement producer and every consumer agree before any implementation begins.
items.context: Entitlements and AI quota currently form a dependency loop between two epics because neither owns the boundary. Publishing the contract first breaks the loop: the quota primitive becomes a contract that the AI harness consumes rather than a feature it waits for.
scope: Plan, feature and entitlement resolution shapes with default deny semantics
Quota reservation, commit and release operations with explicit reconciliation semantics
Subscription lifecycle states covering active, grace, dunning, expired and downgraded
Purchase verification and provider notification shapes
Read-only degradation semantics for over-limit data
Allowed model list per plan and the refusal result for an unlisted model
Request and token quota carried as separate dimensions, each with its unit and measurement point, exactly as T-ADR-ENT-09 fixes them
acceptance_criteria: Entitlement resolution has an explicit deny result; absence of an entitlement is never an implicit allow
A reservation that is never committed is specified to expire and to release without charging
The lifecycle states and their permitted transitions are enumerated so a state machine can be generated from them
The contract states that a downgrade makes excess data read only and never deletes it
Generated clients compile and pass contract verification
Provider notification shapes carry an identifier that makes replay detectable

Entitlement resolution returns an allowed model list, and the contract states that a request naming a model outside that list is refused with its own distinguishable result rather than downgraded to another model
Request quota and token quota are separate dimensions in the schema; neither is derivable from the other and an endpoint that reports only one fails verification
The contract states which dimensions a BYOK request consumes and which it does not, matching T-ADR-ENT-09 rather than restating it differently
Reset boundary and its time zone are carried in the entitlement payload, so a client renders the same boundary the server enforces
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 additions with a worked example of a streaming reservation and reconciliation
Quota dimension vocabulary and model allowlist shape taken from T-ADR-ENT-09; the contract references the record rather than re-deciding it
security_privacy: The contract forbids returning any provider secret or key material
Quota state is server authoritative; the contract exposes no client-writable counter
observability: Contract requires a reservation identifier so metering can be traced end to end
tests: Provider and consumer contract verification
State transition table review
Schema test proving an unlisted-model request has a distinguishable refusal result
Schema test proving request and token dimensions are independently reported
rollout_rollback: Additive publication; the quota interface is frozen before AI consumers implement against it
non_goals: Billing implementation and provider integration, which the api and android tickets own

items.title: Publish the sharing contract for groups, grants, splits and settlements
items.outcome: Group and family sharing is published as a versioned contract whose authorization and redaction semantics are stated in the schema rather than implied by the implementation.
items.context: Sharing decides who can read whose money and is the surface with the highest abuse potential of the three that had no published contract. It is split from the AI tool and administrative contracts so the sharing, AI and admin tracks can be reviewed, published and consumed independently.
scope: Group, membership, grant and revocation shapes with per-member and per-category granularity
Explicit separation of aggregate and detail read permissions in the schema
Split expense, share allocation and settlement shapes with the sum constraint stated
Access transparency log shape readable by the data subject
Counterparty erasure semantics expressed in the shapes rather than left to the implementation
Debt-simplification proposal shape grouped by currency with original-obligation and derivation references
Split-dispute creation, status, evidence-free reason code and resolution shapes
Grant reference bound to the database policy identifier published by T-SEC-01, so a grant reference in the schema names a real enforcement object
Revocation-effectiveness bounds published as part of the contract: the online bound and the offline lease bound, each with its unit and its measurement point
Household aggregate response shapes grouped by currency with fixed closed-period identifiers, snapshot version, completeness state and suppression reason
Joint-goal, per-member contribution and authorized drill-down shapes that never imply a detail grant from an aggregate grant
Aggregate query constraints forbidding arbitrary ranges, exclusion filters and overlapping rolling windows, with rate-limit and privacy-budget refusal results
acceptance_criteria: Aggregate and detail reads are separate operations, not one operation with a flag
A grant shape cannot express a grant to a whole group when the intent is a single member
Split share allocations are specified to sum exactly to the expense amount
The schema forbids returning another user detail data without an explicit grant reference
Generated clients compile and pass contract verification
A simplification proposal cannot mix currencies or mutate original expense and share records
Clients can show how every proposed settlement derives from original obligations
A disputed share has an explicit lifecycle and resolution visible to every authorized member
Every operation that returns another user's detail data carries a grant reference whose value is the identifier of the database policy that admitted it, not a free-text label
A grant reference that names no published policy identifier fails contract verification
The contract publishes a numeric online revocation-effectiveness bound: the maximum interval between a successful revoke call and the first denied read on a server-served request

The contract publishes a numeric offline revocation bound: the maximum lease lifetime an offline client may serve previously granted data for before it must refuse, and states that the two bounds are different numbers and neither may be described as immediate
The contract states that a client which cannot reach the server past its lease expiry must deny rather than serve stale shared data
The same viewer and closed-period query returns the same immutable snapshot; a caller cannot vary a range or exclusion filter to subtract one member or transaction
A suppressed or partial household aggregate is distinguishable from zero and carries no member identity the viewer lacks permission to see
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 additions published as one additive sharing group with its own version
Grant reference type documented as the database policy identifier published by T-SEC-01
Revocation-effectiveness bounds published as machine-readable contract metadata so clients and tests read one number rather than restating prose
Fixed household-period, aggregate snapshot, completeness, joint-goal contribution and privacy-budget refusal schemas
security_privacy: The schema forbids returning another user detail data without an explicit grant reference
Revocation is expressed as a first-class operation rather than an absence of a grant
observability: Contract requires an access event identifier on every detail read so the transparency log can be reconstructed
tests: Provider and consumer contract verification for the sharing group
Schema tests proving no operation exposes detail data without a grant reference
Debt-simplification derivation and currency-separation schema tests
Split-dispute lifecycle contract tests
Schema test proving a grant reference that names no published policy identifier is rejected
Contract test asserting both revocation bounds are present, numeric and distinct
Aggregate differencing contract tests for arbitrary range, overlapping window, exclusion filter, rapid polling and suppressed result
rollout_rollback: Published as one additive group so the sharing track can start without waiting on the AI or admin contracts
non_goals: Implementation of sharing, which the split and family tickets own
AI tool and administrative shapes, which are their own contract tickets

items.title: Publish the deterministic AI tool contract with server-derived user scope
items.outcome: The deterministic AI tool interface is published as a versioned contract in which the user scope is a required, server-derived parameter, so no tool can be specified in a way that lets the model widen its own reach.
items.context: The tool interface decides what the model can reach. Publishing it separately from sharing and administration means the AI track has a frozen boundary to build against without waiting for either of the other two surfaces to be agreed.
scope: Deterministic AI tool interface with user scope derived from authenticated internal caller context and absent from model-controlled arguments
Explicit refusal shape so a tool that cannot answer never returns a partial or approximate result
Provenance identifiers on every returned value so an answer can be traced to the record it came from
Statement that the tool surface is read-only and carries no write operation
acceptance_criteria: Every AI tool operation resolves an authenticated user scope before execution and no model-controlled field can set or widen it
No tool operation in the contract performs a write
A tool result shape carries provenance identifiers alongside every value
The refusal shape is distinguishable from an empty result
Generated clients compile and pass contract verification
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 additions published as one additive AI tool group with its own version
Internal service identity and delegated-subject envelope with audience, issuer, expiry, request binding and replay identifier
security_privacy: Tool responses carry no raw counterparty text beyond the stated policy
The request body has no authoritative user-scope field; subject context is accepted only from the signed internal delegation bound to workload identity
observability: Contract requires a tool name and scope on every call record, without arguments containing personal data
tests: Provider and consumer contract verification for the AI tool group
Schema tests proving no operation omits the required user scope
Contract tests for missing, forged, wrong-audience, expired, replayed and widened delegated subject context

Prompt construction and model routing, which the ai-service tickets own

items.title: Publish the contract for income, budgeting, safe-to-spend, net worth and goals
items.outcome: Income, budgeting, safe-to-spend, net worth and goal shapes are published as one versioned contract with generated clients, so every client renders the same derivations from the same server-computed figures.
items.context: The income, net-worth and goal engines are being built server-side across several api tickets, but no contract exists for any of them yet. Without one, each client would invent its own shape for a safe-to-spend derivation or a net-worth bucket, and the ledger and money-format decision records would have nothing concrete to bind to.
scope: Income model shapes covering salary configuration, expected-versus-received detection and irregular income
Budget and category shapes including rollover across period boundaries
Safe-to-spend and cash-flow forecast shapes including the full derivation inputs
Net-worth snapshot and trend shapes held as separate buckets per currency, with no combined or converted total field
Goal shapes including target, projection, multi-goal competition and the versioned disclaimer identifier
Explicit incomplete-data and unreachable-goal error shapes rather than an empty or optimistic result
Sinking-fund state, contribution schedule and derivation shapes with no ledger-balance field
Salary-market source, range, geography, methodology, as-of date and unavailable or stale result shapes
acceptance_criteria: Every monetary field uses the published money representation and no field is a floating point number
The net-worth shape has no field capable of expressing a combined total across two different currencies
A safe-to-spend or goal response carries enough information for a client to display the derivation without recomputing it
The incomplete-data and unreachable-goal cases have explicit error shapes rather than a silently omitted or optimistic result
Generated Kotlin and TypeScript clients compile and pass contract verification
A sinking-fund response cannot claim an account balance change and a salary-market response cannot omit provenance or freshness
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 additions with examples including a two-currency net-worth response and an unreachable-goal error
security_privacy: No field in any shape permits a cross-user aggregate or benchmark comparison
Salary, budget, net-worth and goal fields are marked for the descriptive-data encryption path defined by the security decision record
observability: Contract requires a computation identifier on every derived response so a support query can trace a figure
tests: Provider and consumer contract verification
Example validation against the schema including the two-currency and incomplete-data cases
Sinking-fund no-ledger-effect and salary-market provenance schema tests
rollout_rollback: Additive publication under the expand and contract protocol; consumers pin a version
non_goals: Engine implementation, which the api income, net-worth and goal tickets own
Currency conversion or any combined cross-currency total, which stays out of scope until the globalization epic (E30) delivers a conversion path

items.title: Publish the shared statement-import contract components
items.outcome: Preview, commit, column mapping, row error, idempotency, confidence band and dedup outcome are published once as shared contract components, so statement import, cross-channel deduplication and every client review screen use one shape instead of three.
items.context: api#10 currently carries its import preview inline in the API ticket, api#18 invents its own confidence and duplicate reporting for cross-channel deduplication, and T-CON-02 adds a third for categorisation. Three encodings of the same idea means three client renderings, three sets of tests and a guaranteed divergence the first time a band is renamed. Import is also the ingestion mitigation entirely within our control, so its review screen is a trust surface, not a utility.
scope: Import preview component: per-row action, reason, source row number and the counts that summarise it
Import commit component: what was created, skipped and rejected, with a stable reference to the preview it came from
Column mapping component: institution preset, detected columns, user overrides and unmapped columns
Row error component: position, machine-readable reason code and a human message that carries no raw account identifier
Idempotency semantics for preview and commit, keyed so a repeated commit of the same preview is a no-op
Confidence band component with a fixed vocabulary rather than a free numeric scale reinvented per endpoint
Dedup outcome component naming the matched record, the match basis and the source precedence that decided it
acceptance_criteria: Preview and commit are separate operations and a commit references the preview it was produced from; a commit with no preview reference is rejected by the schema
Committing the same preview reference twice is specified as a no-op that returns the original result rather than importing again
The confidence band vocabulary is closed and shared; an endpoint that returns a band outside it fails contract verification
The dedup outcome names the matched record, the basis of the match and the precedence rule applied, so a client can explain a skipped row without a second call
The row error reason codes are enumerated and no reason code carries a raw account number or a full statement line
Generated Kotlin, TypeScript and Python clients compile against these components and pass contract verification
api#10 and api#18 both reference these components; a locally declared preview, confidence or dedup shape fails verification
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 components published as one additive import group with its own version
Components are referenced, never copied: an endpoint that inlines an equivalent shape fails the lint rule this ticket adds
security_privacy: No component carries raw statement file content, and the row error message is specified to exclude full account identifiers
The preview reference is unguessable and scoped to its owner, so one user cannot commit another user's preview
observability: The counts in the preview and commit components are the same counts the import metrics record, so a client total and a server metric cannot disagree
tests: Provider and consumer contract verification for the import group across all three generated clients
Schema test proving a commit without a preview reference is rejected
Lint test proving an inlined duplicate of a shared component fails
rollout_rollback: Published additively ahead of api#10, so the API ticket consumes the components rather than inventing them
Rollback is unpublishing the component group before any consumer pins it; after that, the expand-migrate-contract protocol applies
non_goals: Import implementation, parsing and institution presets, which api#10 owns
Cross-channel deduplication logic, which api#18 owns
Category inference, which T-CON-02 and the ingestion tickets own

items.title: Publish the export, consent, rights-request and transparency contract
items.outcome: Data export, the consent and purpose registry, data-principal rights requests and their status, and the user-visible transparency payload are published as one versioned contract, so the compliance floor, the Android trust surfaces and the web trust centre implement the same shapes rather than three private ones.
items.context: The compliance floor, the Android trust controls and the web trust centre all read and write the same four things - what a user consented to, what they asked us to do about their data, how far that request has got, and what we did with their data - and none of them has a published shape for any of it. Export in particular is a legal obligation with a format consequence: a versioned CSV and JSON export is a promise about column stability, and a promise nobody wrote down is one nobody can keep across a schema change.
scope: Versioned export contract: the CSV column set and the JSON document shape, their version identifier, and the compatibility rule for adding or removing a column
Export request, progress and delivery shapes, including expiry of a generated artifact
Consent and purpose registry shapes: purpose identifier, version, grant and withdrawal events, and the evidence recorded with each
Data-principal rights request shapes: request type, submission, acknowledgement, status transitions, outcome and refusal reason
Status shape carrying the statutory clock: when the request started, what the response deadline is and how much of it remains
Transparency payload shape: what was accessed, by which class of actor, under which purpose, and when
Nominee and grievance-contact shapes so a rights request can be raised on behalf of a data principal
Explicit export exclusion for every device-local raw-event field, including the raw-message HMAC and parser diagnostic state
acceptance_criteria: The export contract carries an explicit format version, and adding a column is specified as additive while removing one requires the expand-migrate-contract path with a stated compatibility window
The CSV and JSON exports are specified to contain the same content, so a client cannot be told the two formats differ in what they include
A consent record names its purpose identifier and purpose version, and a withdrawal references the exact grant it withdraws rather than a purpose in general
A rights request has an enumerated type, an enumerated status set and defined transitions, so a state machine can be generated from the contract
The status shape exposes the response deadline and the time remaining, so a client cannot compute a different clock from the server
A refused rights request carries an enumerated refusal reason; a free-text-only refusal fails the schema
The transparency payload never carries administrative identity or an internal reason code outside the published vocabulary
Generated Kotlin, TypeScript and Python clients compile against the contract and pass verification
The export manifest contains structured transactions and source identifiers but cannot name or carry the device-local raw-message digest
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 additions published as one additive privacy group with its own version, plus the CSV column manifest as machine-readable data
Purpose identifiers and rights-request types are closed vocabularies referenced by the compliance implementation rather than restated in it
security_privacy: An export artifact reference is unguessable, scoped to its owner and expires; the contract states the expiry as a required field
The transparency payload is specified as subject-visible, which fixes what it may never contain: administrative identity, another user's identity, or key material
A rights request shape carries no authentication material and no session token
observability: The status shape is the same data the compliance service reports on, so an overdue request is visible from the contract-level field rather than an internal metric only
tests: Provider and consumer contract verification for the privacy group across all three generated clients
Schema test proving a withdrawal without a grant reference is rejected
Schema test proving a refusal without an enumerated reason is rejected
Export manifest test proving the CSV column set and the JSON shape declare the same content
Negative export-schema fixture proving raw_hash and message_digest are forbidden
rollout_rollback: Published additively ahead of the compliance floor implementation, so T-CMP-01 consumes the shapes rather than inventing them
Rollback is unpublishing the group before a consumer pins it; afterwards the expand-migrate-contract protocol applies, and the export format version makes a client's expectation explicit
non_goals: Compliance implementation, retention jobs and the consent ledger itself, which E27 owns
Client surfaces, which the Android and web trust tickets own
Legal interpretation of any obligation, which the counsel-reviewed jurisdiction profile owns

The administrative audit stream and its relationship to this subject-visible transparency stream, which T-ADR-ADMIN-06 decides; this contract publishes the subject-visible stream only and may never carry administrative identity

items.title: Publish the messaging preference, device and support request contract
items.outcome: Messaging preferences, device registration, delivery status, and support request creation and status are published as one versioned contract, so the notification service, both clients and the support surfaces agree on the shapes before any of them is built.
items.context: Two unowned systems are referenced across the plan without a schema: something that decides whether a user may be messaged, and something that receives a support request. Without published shapes the notification service and the clients would each invent their own preference model, and the help links already described in the trust and onboarding tickets would point at nothing. Publishing the contract first is what lets the api, android and web work start in parallel.
scope: Message class vocabulary shared by the server and both clients, closed rather than free-text
Per-class preference shapes with an explicit opt-out and an unsubscribe reference that works without a session
Quiet-hours shape with its time zone, and the rule for a message that becomes deliverable after quiet hours end
Device registration, refresh and deregistration shapes with a platform discriminator
Delivery status shape covering queued, sent, delivered, suppressed and failed, with a machine-readable suppression reason
Support request creation, category, status transitions and message thread shapes
Support attachment reference shape with its retention and expiry declared in the contract
acceptance_criteria: The message class vocabulary is closed; a preference or a delivery record naming an unknown class fails verification
Every message class carries an explicit user preference, and the contract states that the absence of a preference is not consent for a class that requires one
The unsubscribe reference is usable without an authenticated session and is scoped to one class and one recipient
Suppression is a first-class delivery outcome with an enumerated reason, so a suppressed message is distinguishable from a failed one
